# SoundObjects overview

A SoundObject represents a musical idea on the [Score](score.qmd): a note, a
phrase, a pattern, or a section containing other ideas. The Score places that
idea in time; the object supplies material for Blue to turn into Csound score
events. Choose the object type that fits how you want to work with the idea.

## Choose and place an object

Right-click an empty part of a SoundObject layer and open **Add SoundObject**.
The menu includes **GenericScore** for Csound score text, **PianoRoll** for
drawn notes, **PatternObject** for pattern material, and **PolyObject** for a
nested timeline. [AudioFile](audio-file.qmd) refers to an audio file. An
**AudioClip** on an audio layer has a separate timeline and editor workflow.
For the other available types, see [More SoundObject types](soundobject-types.qmd).

The object appears at the point you clicked. With **Snap** on, placement and
later dragging follow the selected snap division. Click an object to select
it, Shift-click to add or remove it from the selection, or drag across empty
Score space to select a group. Drag a selected object to move it; drag its
left or right edge to change its position or width. The [Time](time.qmd)
chapter explains ruler, snap, and time-base choices.

Double-click a selected ordinary SoundObject to open its type-specific
editor. Double-clicking a **PolyObject** enters its nested Score instead; use
the Score path at the top to return to the parent timeline. Right-click a
selected object for actions such as **Cut**, **Copy**, **Remove**, **Set
Color…**, **Set Subjective Time to Objective Time**, and **Add to Project
SoundObjects**. Right-click empty Score space to add or paste an object.

## Read its shared properties

With one object selected, **Score Object Properties** shows its **Name**,
**Start Time**, **Subjective Duration**, calculated **End Time**, and
**Color**. Start Time says where the object begins. Subjective Duration is
the width shown on the Score; End Time is read-only, calculated from start
plus duration, and displayed in the Start Time format. The editable time fields have their own format
menus, so an object can use beats, bars, seconds, or other supported formats
independently of the ruler.

Where the object supports them, the properties panel also shows **Time
Behavior**, **Use Repeat Point**, **Repeat Point**, and **Note Processors**.
The repeat-point controls apply to repeat modes. The color changes how the
object appears on the Score; it does not alter the generated notes.

## Relate width to generated notes

A SoundObject's visible width and the length of the notes it generates are
different concepts. For objects with a Time Behavior control:

| Behavior             | Effect on generated notes                                                                            |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Scale**            | Stretches or compresses note starts and lengths to fit the subjective duration.                      |
| **Repeat**           | Repeats the material to fill that duration and clips notes at each repeat boundary.                  |
| **Repeat (Classic)** | Repeats full cycles; in the final partial cycle, includes only notes that fit entirely.              |
| **None**             | Leaves the generated note times as written, even when they extend beyond the object's visible width. |

For repeat modes, **Use Repeat Point** and **Repeat Point** set the cycle
length when supported. If no repeat point is used, the generated material's
length supplies the cycle. The available behavior and default vary by object
type; an AudioFile SoundObject, for example, does not use the note-scaling
behavior.

For a **GenericScore**, event times in its text are relative to the object's
start. The [First project](first-project.qmd) example `i1 0 4 0.15 440`
starts at the object's beginning. Moving the object later offsets that event
in the generated score. Blue applies the object's Note Processors to its
initial notes, then its Time Behavior, then its Score start offset. A
SoundObject layer and the Score can each apply further processor chains to
their combined notes. See [Note Processors](note-processors.qmd) for those
scopes.

Some types contribute more than score notes to the generated CSD. AudioFile
and FrozenObject reference audio files; Sound creates a synthesis instrument;
LineObject and ZakLineObject generate supporting control material. Use
**Generate CSD to Screen** to inspect the complete result before depending on
a generated table, UDO, or other resource.

## Render from the middle of a project

Blue passes the overlap between the render range and each contributing object
as offsets from that object's start. Ordinary note-producing objects cannot
resume a note that began before the selected range, so that note may be
omitted even if it overlaps the range. These types generate their own clipped
event or control interval:

| Type              | Generated behavior for a range that starts inside the object                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Sound**         | Starts a shortened event for its BSB instrument at the overlap start. It does not pass an audio-file seek offset, so this is a new instrument event rather than continuation of an already-running voice.                                                                                                                                |
| **AudioFile**     | Starts a shortened `diskin2` event and passes the overlap offset converted to clip-relative seconds through the project tempo map. The instrument refers to the selected audio file path; the file is not embedded in the CSD. If **Copy Imported Media** is enabled, Blue copies a newly selected file into the project's media folder. |
| **LineObject**    | Starts a shortened event and uses normalized start and end positions to sample the corresponding section of its line table. It writes the resulting control value to its `gk` variable.                                                                                                                                                  |
| **ZakLineObject** | Starts a shortened event and uses normalized start and end positions to sample the corresponding section of its line table, writing values to the configured zak channel.                                                                                                                                                                |
| **FrozenObject**  | Starts a shortened `diskin2` event, referring to its stored freeze file and passing the overlap offset converted to clip-relative seconds through the project tempo map. The nested source object is retained for unfreezing; playback reads the freeze file.                                                                            |

The AudioFile and FrozenObject generators convert the beat-domain overlap
offset to object-relative seconds using the project's tempo map:
`seconds(objectStart + offset) - seconds(objectStart)`. This is the unit that
[`diskin2`](https://csound.com/manual/opcodes/diskin2/)'s skip-time input
expects. Sync/async tests cover direct AudioFile and FrozenObject placements,
direct Instances of those file-backed objects (including nonzero source
starts), and file objects under nested PolyObjects with unscaled, unrepeated
timing. For a linked Instance, Blue can also translate the selected window
before SoundLayer pruning when both the linked Instance and its flat PolyObject
source use `TimeBehavior.NONE` and have no Note Processor chains, no source
SoundLayer has a Note Processor chain, and every active direct child reports a
range-independent origin. GenericScore origins qualify only when all parsed
notes fit inside the object's subjective duration. Sync/async model tests
cover a source event at beat 2, file leaves at beat 4, and selected range
`[3,5]`: the SoundLayer is queried over `[5,7]`, while each file generator
receives its object-relative `[1,3]` overlap; the seek is one beat and the
duration is two beats. This is a Blue 3 extension to Java
Blue's positional linked-source range handling. Dynamic JavaScript/Python
sources, nested containers, transformed or repeated sources, processor-bearing
compositions, and sources whose events extend outside their declared span do
not provide a safe origin and keep the existing behavior. For example, an
event at beat 2 in a GenericScore with subjective duration 2 does not establish
an origin: when the selected range starts at beat 3, SoundLayer prunes that
score object by its declared duration, and file leaves retain the legacy seek
and duration. This out-of-span case needs a separate range-aware contract.
Direct AudioFile selected-range playback has been heard in a built macOS app
with a tempo change. A packaged run also froze an AudioFile and produced a
selected-range FrozenObject render matching the direct render; realtime
playback started and finished, and the user accepted the captured output. See
[Rendering](rendering.qmd) for choosing a range.

For editing each kind, see [GenericScore](generic-score.qmd),
[PianoRoll](piano-roll.qmd), [PatternObject](pattern-object.qmd), and
[PolyObjects](polyobjects.qmd). For reusable material, see
[SoundObject Library](soundobject-library.qmd) and [Instance](instance.qmd).
An Instance is a Score placement linked to a project-library definition; an
independent copy is edited separately.
